title: Red Means Stop!
hook: The Car Parade is across the big road — and Brian wants to RUN. Can the team learn how signals keep everyone safe?
core_lesson: Near roads, we stop at the {kerb}, follow the signals, look and listen — and always cross with a grown-up.
adult_safety_note: This episode models crossing ONLY with a supervising adult, holding hands, at a signal-controlled {crossing}. It does not teach children to cross alone. Road rules are localised for {name}; they are simplified and have not yet been reviewed by a local road-safety expert.

learning_objectives.goal: Stop at the {kerb}, hold a grown-up's hand, and cross only with a grown-up.
Car lights tell drivers what to do; in {name} they go {sequenceText}.
The pedestrian signal is for walkers: wait for the {walk}, even when the road looks empty.
In {name} traffic drives on the {side}, so the nearest cars come from the {look1}: look {look1}, {look2}, {look1} again.
Put the car-light pattern in order, starting from red.
Brian chooses patience: he waits for the team instead of running ahead.

talk_together: Why did the team wait for the {walk} even when the road looked empty?
Next time you walk near a road with a grown-up, can you spot the {crossing} and the signals?
Which way do we look first here, and why?

complete.recall: Stop at the {kerb}. Follow the signals. Cross with a grown-up!
complete.question: On your next walk with a grown-up, point out every traffic light and {crossing} you see.

ng.label: Nigeria
ng.name: Nigeria
ng.review: Not yet reviewed by a Nigerian road-safety expert (FRSC guidance should be checked). Last checked against public sources on 2026-10-16.

vars.note: Some signals may also show red and amber together before green, and signal types vary by city — confirm with FRSC guidance.

ca.label: Canada
ca.name: Canada
ca.review: Not yet reviewed by a Canadian road-safety expert. Rules vary by province. Last checked against public sources on 2026-10-16.

vars.note: Many crossings have countdown timers; don't start crossing once the hand is showing. In Québec, stop signs may say ARRÊT.

gb.label: United Kingdom
gb.name: the UK
gb.review: Not yet reviewed by a UK road-safety expert. Last checked against public sources on 2026-10-16.

vars.note: Car lights show red and amber together before green. Signal-controlled crossings (pelican, puffin, toucan) have a green figure; zebra crossings have stripes and flashing amber beacons.

fr.label: France
fr.name: France
fr.review: Not yet reviewed by a French road-safety expert. Last checked against public sources on 2026-10-16.

vars.note: The crossing is called a passage piéton. Car lights go red → green → orange, without a red-and-orange phase.

de.label: Germany
de.name: Germany
de.review: Not yet reviewed by a German road-safety expert. Last checked against public sources on 2026-10-16.

vars.note: The crossing is called a Zebrastreifen; the pedestrian figure is often the Ampelmännchen. Car lights show red and yellow together before green.

au.label: Australia
au.name: Australia
au.review: Not yet reviewed by an Australian road-safety expert. Rules vary slightly by state. Last checked against public sources on 2026-10-16.

vars.note: Press the button once. Never start crossing on a flashing or steady red figure; if you are already crossing when it starts flashing, keep going safely.

cn.label: China
cn.name: China
cn.review: Not yet reviewed by a Chinese road-safety expert. Applies to mainland China only. Last checked against public sources on 2026-10-16.

vars.note: Rules shown are for mainland China; Hong Kong and Macau drive on the left. Many signals have countdown timers. Stop signs show 停.

us.label: United States
us.name: the US
us.review: Not yet reviewed by a US road-safety expert. Rules vary by state and city. Last checked against public sources on 2026-10-16.

vars.note: Many crossings have countdown timers. A flashing hand means don't start crossing. Car lights have no red-and-yellow phase.

season.title: The Mystery of the Missing Wheels

interactions.label: Light-pattern puzzle
interactions.prompt: Starting with red, put the car lights in order for {name}.
interactions.hint: Start with red — that's where the pattern begins.
interactions.explain: In {name}: {sequenceText}, then back to red again. {Amber} means the light is about to change.

interactions.label: Wait or go?
interactions.prompt: The {dontwalk} is showing, but the road looks empty. What do we do?

options.text: Wait with our grown-up for the {walk}.

interactions.hint: Cars can appear very quickly. Who does the signal say should wait?
interactions.explain: We wait for the {walk}, with our grown-up, even when the road looks empty. Cars can come fast!

interactions.label: Look which way?
interactions.prompt: In {name}, cars drive on the {side}. Which way do we look first?
interactions.hint: The nearest lane of cars comes toward us first. Which side is it coming from when cars drive on the {side}?
interactions.explain: Look {look1} first — the nearest cars come from there. Then look {look2}, then {look1} again, and keep listening.

interactions.label: Safest place to cross
interactions.prompt: Where is the safest place to cross the road?

options.text: At the {crossing}, holding a grown-up's hand.

interactions.hint: Where can drivers see us clearly, and where do the signals help?
interactions.explain: At the {crossing}, with a grown-up: drivers can see us and the signals help everyone take turns.

panels.visual: Brian bounces with excitement about the Car Parade; Jasmine reminds him about the big road.
panels.caption: Saturday: the Sunbeam Junction Car Parade!

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: The Car Parade is in the park! Let's RUN!

dialogue.speaker: Jasmine
dialogue.text: But the park is across the big road.

panels.alt_text: In the garage, Brian jumps with excitement. Jasmine holds up a hand, thinking about the big road.

panels.visual: Ada sets the rule: walk together and hold hands near roads.

dialogue.speaker: Ada
dialogue.text: We'll walk together. Near roads, you hold a grown-up's hand.

dialogue.speaker: Marcus
dialogue.text: Hold hands!

panels.alt_text: Auntie Ada holds out her hand. Marcus grabs it happily.

panels.visual: On the street, Brian has hurried ahead; Ada calls him to stop at the edge.
panels.caption: New word: {KERB} — the edge of the {pavement}, next to the road. We always stop there.

dialogue.speaker: Ada
dialogue.text: Brian, stop at the {kerb} and wait for us.

panels.alt_text: A busy street with shops and a road. Brian has hurried ahead along the {pavement}; Auntie Ada, Jasmine and Marcus are behind him.

panels.visual: Brian stops at the edge of the pavement and waits.

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: Okay. I'll stop and wait for my team.

panels.alt_text: Brian stands still at the edge of the {pavement}, hands by his sides, waiting for the others.

panels.visual: Jasmine notices the traffic light for cars changing.

dialogue.speaker: Jasmine
dialogue.text: That light keeps changing. It's a pattern!

panels.alt_text: Jasmine points up at a traffic light beside the road. It is showing red.

panels.visual: Ada explains the car lights.
panels.caption: Lights for cars.

dialogue.speaker: Ada
dialogue.text: Car lights tell drivers what to do. Red means stop. Green means go.

panels.alt_text: Auntie Ada points at the car traffic light, now showing green. Jasmine watches closely.

fact.title: Car lights in {name}
fact.text: Here, car lights go {sequenceText}, then back to red. {Amber} means the light is about to change, so drivers get ready to stop.

panels.visual: Jasmine watches the light go round the pattern again.

dialogue.speaker: Jasmine
dialogue.text: I'll watch it go round again and remember the order!

panels.alt_text: Jasmine stares at the traffic light, now showing {amber}, counting the colours on her fingers.

panels.visual: Marcus presses the crossing button again and again; Ada smiles.

dialogue.speaker: Marcus
dialogue.text: Press! Press! PRESS!

dialogue.speaker: Ada
dialogue.text: Once is enough, Marcus. The signal heard you!

panels.alt_text: Marcus jabs the button on the crossing signal pole over and over. BEEP! Auntie Ada laughs.

panels.visual: Ada points to the pedestrian signal showing 'wait'.

dialogue.speaker: Ada
dialogue.text: This light is for us. The {dontwalk} means wait.

panels.alt_text: The pedestrian signal shows a {dontwalk}. Auntie Ada points at it; Brian looks up.

panels.visual: The road looks empty. Brian wants to go; Ada explains why they wait.

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: There are no cars! Can we just go?

dialogue.speaker: Ada
dialogue.text: We still wait for the {walk}. Cars can come quickly.

panels.alt_text: The road behind them is empty. Brian leans forward impatiently. Auntie Ada keeps hold of his hand and shakes her head kindly.

panels.visual: The pedestrian signal changes to 'go'; the cars have stopped before the crossing.

dialogue.speaker: Ada
dialogue.text: The {walk} is on. Now we stop, look and listen.

panels.alt_text: The pedestrian signal now shows a {walk}. Cars have stopped on both sides of the {crossing}. Auntie Ada stands at the {kerb}.

panels.visual: Brian asks which way to look first; Ada explains the driving side.

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: Which way do we look first?

dialogue.speaker: Ada
dialogue.text: In {name}, cars drive on the {side}. Look {look1} first!

panels.alt_text: Brian looks up at Auntie Ada with a question. She points to the {look1}, where the nearest cars come from.

panels.visual: Everyone at the kerb looks the correct way first.
panels.caption: Look {look1}, then {look2}, then {look1} again. Listen, too!
panels.alt_text: Brian, Jasmine, Marcus and Auntie Ada stand together at the {kerb}, all turning their eyes to the {look1} first.

panels.visual: Holding hands, the family walks across the crossing while cars wait.
panels.caption: Hold hands. Walk, don't run. Keep looking and listening.

dialogue.speaker: Jasmine
dialogue.text: We're crossing together!

panels.alt_text: Auntie Ada leads Brian, Jasmine and Marcus across the {crossing}, all holding hands, while the cars wait.

panels.visual: Safe on the other side; parade cars roll past on the road.
panels.caption: Safe at the park — just in time for the Car Parade!

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: We made it. Together!

dialogue.speaker: Marcus
dialogue.text: PARADE!

panels.alt_text: Safe on the {pavement}, the children cheer as colourful parade cars roll past on the road.

panels.visual: Ada points at a stop sign; Jasmine studies its shape.
panels.caption: An eight-sided red sign means STOP.

dialogue.speaker: Ada
dialogue.text: Lights, signs and crossings help everyone share the road.

dialogue.speaker: Jasmine
dialogue.text: That sign has eight sides!

panels.alt_text: Beside the road stands a red eight-sided stop sign. Jasmine counts its sides while Auntie Ada smiles.

panels.visual: Brian thinks about the safest place to cross.

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: So where's the safest place to cross?

panels.alt_text: Brian looks along the street at the {crossing}, thinking.

panels.visual: Marcus pretends to be a stop sign; Jasmine laughs.

dialogue.speaker: Marcus
dialogue.text: Me a STOP sign!

dialogue.speaker: Jasmine
dialogue.text: You're the cutest stop sign ever!

panels.alt_text: Marcus stands very straight with both hands up like a stop sign. Jasmine giggles.

panels.visual: Walking home, Brian and Jasmine remind each other of the rules.
panels.caption: Walking home.

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: Remember, team: stop at the {kerb}.

dialogue.speaker: Jasmine
dialogue.text: And wait for the {walk}!

panels.alt_text: On the walk home, Brian and Jasmine stop at the {kerb} and remind each other of the rules.

panels.visual: Marcus adds his rule; Ada praises the team.

dialogue.speaker: Marcus
dialogue.text: And HOLD HANDS!

dialogue.speaker: Ada
dialogue.text: Road-safety stars! And a grown-up always comes with you near roads.

panels.alt_text: Marcus holds Auntie Ada's hand tightly and beams. Ada smiles proudly.

panels.visual: Back in the garage, the children build a cardboard road for Bolt.

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: Let's build a road for Bolt — with a {crossing}!

dialogue.speaker: Jasmine
dialogue.text: I'll make a paper traffic light.

panels.alt_text: In the garage, Brian lays out a cardboard road on the floor. Jasmine holds up a small paper traffic light she has drawn.

panels.visual: Marcus holds up the paper red light; Bolt stops right on time.

dialogue.speaker: Marcus
dialogue.text: RED! Bolt STOP!

panels.alt_text: Marcus holds the paper traffic light showing red. Bolt has stopped on the cardboard road just before it.

panels.visual: Brian and Jasmine sum up the safety rules.

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: Stop at the {kerb}. Look {look1} first. Cross with a grown-up.

dialogue.speaker: Jasmine
dialogue.text: And follow the lights!

panels.alt_text: Brian and Jasmine stand proudly beside their cardboard road and paper traffic light.

panels.visual: That night, Bolt won't move again — and there is no thread this time.
panels.caption: Next time: The Battery Mystery!

dialogue.speaker: Brian
dialogue.text: Bolt won't go again… and this time there's no thread!

dialogue.speaker: Jasmine
dialogue.text: A new mystery!

panels.alt_text: In the evening garage, Brian kneels beside Bolt, which sits still with its switch on. Jasmine leans in, curious.
